claims.text: An ab initio multiscale framework can separately predict lattice and electronic heat transport in HfNbTaTiZr below 200 K.
The framework can predict total thermal conductivity in HfNbTaTiZr containing approximately 1 wt.% oxygen from 300 to 1200 K.
The framework will have at least 50% lower prediction error than earlier Debye-based or perfect-crystal models.
Variations in atomic mass and force constants affect phonon dispersion in HfNbTaTiZr.
Oxygen impurities introduce point defects that affect phonon transport and electron scattering in HfNbTaTiZr.
Explicitly separating lattice and electronic contributions overcomes limitations associated with Debye-temperature approximations and perfect-crystal assumptions.
Representing anharmonic and impurity scattering produces a more realistic description of thermal-transport processes.
More realistic treatment of scattering and separate transport channels will lower prediction error by at least 50%.
Below 200 K, lattice and electronic heat-transport contributions in HfNbTaTiZr are comparable.
Between 300 and 1200 K, HfNbTaTiZr containing approximately 1 wt.% oxygen has total thermal conductivity in the range 10–17 W/(K m).
Previous analytical models and simulations rely on single-Debye-temperature approximations and perfect, defect-free crystals.
Previous models conflate or inadequately separate lattice and electronic thermal-transport contributions.
The reliability of DFT calculations and impurity-scattering parameterization limits the accuracy of the proposed approach.
The quantitative effect of 1 wt.% oxygen on scattering in HfNbTaTiZr is uncertain.
The extent of anharmonic interactions in HfNbTaTiZr at high temperature is uncertain.
